title: Poilievre claims constituent's job was threatened after meeting at CFB Wainwright
summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre says one of his constituents — a nurse who helped treat soldiers burned in the CFB Wainwright fire — is having her employment threatened because she met with him.

image.caption: This photo of nurse Maureen Carpenter was posted online by Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre on Oct. 20, 2026. (Pierre Poilievre/Facebook)

blocks.text: Politics·New
Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre says one of his constituents — a nurse who helped treat soldiers burned in the CFB Wainwright fire — is having her employment threatened because she met with him.
Nurse treating soldiers is being harassed, Opposition leader says in House of Commons
In an unusual speech in the House of Commons on Wednesday evening, Poilievre said his parliamentary privilege is being breached.

Last month, Maureen Carpenter was photographed speaking to Poilievre following the fire that killed five soldiers and wounded 38 others on Oct. 17. Poilievre said she is under contract with Calian Health, a government contractor, and works as a nurse.

"Maureen spoke to me on base, with the permission of the unit commander. I had the permission of the base commander to be there. She talked about caring for our men and women on the shift that night, that horrendous night," said Poilievre.

An online post from Oct. 20 shows Poilievre meeting with medical staff at CFB Wainwright Health Services. Online comments identify the woman in the photo as Carpenter, which was confirmed by Poilievre's office.
(Pierre Poilievre/Facebook)

"We owe Maureen as well as colleagues like her, our greatest gratitude. That is what I conveyed in our conversation. Instead, Maureen tells me that she's been threatened by Calian Health, all because she spoke to her local member of Parliament."
Poilievre is the MP for Wainwright, Alta., residents. The base is part of his federal riding of Battle River-Crowfoot.

He said, following the meeting, Carpenter was subject to a complaint and threatened — told by her boss that if her term contract was not already coming to an end, she would be put under the microscope by the company's legal department.
"The implicit message was that her contract would no longer have any chance of renewal, something that she had taken for granted before that point," Poilievre said.
Neither Calian nor Carpenter responded immediately to a request for comment.

Poilievre said Carpenter was told she violated the company's policy by meeting with her MP. He said there is no such policy — there is a rule against speaking to the media, but nothing prohibiting speaking to a member of Parliament.
'My intention was not for this to be politicized': Poilievre raises rare point of privilege

He said being able to speak to an MP is a right guaranteed under the Charter, and a requirement in order to ensure Canadians get good government. During the conversation, he said they discussed better support for mental health following the fires.
He said they did not discuss her company or workplace.
Poilievre said that when he heard from Carpenter, he raised the issue with the minister responsible. His office later confirmed he meant Defence Minister David McGuinty.
McGuinty's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
"My intention was not for this to be politicized. I simply wanted it to be solved," Poilievre said.
"Based on his original assurances, I had hoped the minister would put Calian in its place … but her family is indicating that the problems have worsened and there is no end in sight."
Poilievre moved a motion to refer the matter to the procedure and House affairs committee for investigation.

"Ideally though, the government and Calian will instead simply say sorry and fix the problem," he said. "But until and unless that happens, my ability to represent my constituents has been interfered with and you must denounce this conduct."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

She previously worked for CBC’s The Fifth Estate and in the Halifax, Montreal and Charlottetown newsrooms. Her investigative and breaking news coverage has won five RTDNA awards.
